title: The Prison of Fog
subtitle: What lies beyond the exquisitely crafted cage of mist?

items.text: The Story of Oliver
The Prison of Fog
I can't remember when it was that I began to hate the fog.
This city, forever shrouded in fog, prompts the overwrought comparison between Sisyphus's endless struggle and our own.
The fog that covers this absurdity and unsightliness is like a bell jar imprisoning a cricket.
Beyond those invisible intangible borders lie the jeering faces of the gods. They drained every ounce of vitality from the cricket, dispatching the fog as their most faithful instrument.
And so, the cricket turned its head to find this thick fog everywhere—up, down, left, right—all around. No escape in sight, no perceptible boundaries... Even its cry would be lost in the fog.

That fog as viscous as snot flowing from a runny nose enveloped the cricket to the point where the poor wretch couldn't even make a sound. It rubbed its wings in vain, attempting to make even the slightest noise, but the only thing that filled the air was the fog and its silent ridicule.

To this day, no one has responded to its pleas. In this thick fog, there is only silence, the silence of death... That's what it does, this fog—it invariably forces the individual to face the certainty of their own demise.
Walking in this endless fog, with no end in sight, surrounded by a cage of untouchable wire, where even the most furious strikes have no means of finding their target.
The only thing one is allowed to feel is extreme loneliness and that deathly still.
We, walking through this dense fog for the sake of our so-called mission, might possibly be the most pitiable crickets of all.
How long has it been since I last saw the sun?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Oliver Fog?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Oh... Sorry, Miss Vertin. I lost myself for a moment there. What were we talking about just now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That we hoped you would aid our cause two days from now. With the enemy well hidden within the fog;  determining their location will be no easy feat. It looks like we'll be counting on you and your arcane skill to succeed.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: The day after tomorrow... That's a holiday, isn't it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It is indeed.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Before I offer you a response, Miss Vertin, allow me to ask a question. Who was it that proposed I join you in this operation of yours?
It was Mr. Knight.

branch.speaker: Oliver Fog
branch.text: And will he also be taking part?

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Mr. Knight will not be taking part in this operation, but he recommended you wholeheartedly.

branch.speaker: Oliver Fog
branch.text: You do know that he's egging me on by passing this work to me? It's quite evident, Miss Vertin.

items.text: And what if I were to say I was the one that chose you, recommendations notwithstanding?
items.edge_label: …計画したのはわたしだから

branch.speaker: Oliver Fog
branch.text: Deception is not your strong suit. It's entirely obvious that you're covering for him.

branch.speaker: Oliver Fog
branch.text: You know for a fact that I am not the kind to work on a day off, and based on your personality, which is shall we say; conciliatory in nature, you would never have proposed such a plan.

branch.speaker: Oliver Fog
branch.text: So, then. The suit of armor put you up to this? Am I right?

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: .....Perhaps. But why would you suspect him in the first place?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Miss Vertin, I intend to direct a formal complaint towards Mr. Knight.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Allow me to come straight to the point, Miss Vertin. I would be more than willing to help you in any way, merely due to the goodwill we have fostered through the course of our acquaintance. However, my principles will not permit me to sacrifice my hard-earned time off merely for the convenience of others.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I will provide you with any advice you may require, but my practical assistance is out of the question.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So then, this your latest experiment in reformist rhetoric?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Not at all. It's a manner of prevarication that's been in use since Chamberlain's day.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Look— I won't try to force you, Oliver. I'm merely here to discuss the matter with you.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Then I thank you for your understanding, Miss Vertin. If there's nothing else I can help you with, I will take my leave. there's work I've yet to finish today.
Somewhere in the Suitcase

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: What someone is about to recount to you is a sworn testimonial of a face-to-face run-in with a dark spirit, a blood-thirsty creature of undeath someone encountered as a chivalrous knight long, long ago.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Brilliant! I love this story— I mean, Miss Sotheby knows she's definitely going to love this story!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone came across a long-abandoned castle with a close friend while journeying the countryside one dark night.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hm...

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: ...The forest around the castle was a mire shrouded in eerie mist, and someone was traipsing right through it, boots tramping on rotten leaves and kicking up the most vile, putrid stink of rancid soil mixed with the damp stench of decay.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But our destination was not far off. We had almost reached the castle gate.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Suddenly, someone and that faithful friend spied a shadowy figure up ahead. He was slumped askew against a tree, seemingly unconscious.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Back then, someone was still a simple-minded knight. Someone stepped forward and went heedlessly over to the side of the mysterious figure...
Just as everyone leans in closer, listening ever more attentively to the knight's story, another figure passes by.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I can confirm that there are no problems with the work plan. Everything seems to be in order... The schedule is a little tight, but if we proceed accordingly, we can still finish all work on time today.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone tapped him on the shoulder, but he didn't budge an inch. Then, someone tapped him again...

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: He suddenly lifted his head to reveal a ghastly, desiccated face with black holes where his eyes should've been!

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Miss Sotheby knows! It must've been the Chupacabra!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: If only the truth were so simple. As soon as we saw that living corpse, someone and someone's good friend knew right away—

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: In the depths of the castle lay a terrifying, treacherous, blood-curdling banshee!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: An evil spirit? What a surprise! All the spirits Miss Sotheby has met have been most cordial to her! Though to be fair. I have never had the misfortune of meeting a thirsty one before.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That's a good point... They might be a bit on the quirky side, but Poltergeist and Click are good souls.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Excuse me please, some of us have work to do.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, this way, please—from my side, over here.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Mr. Fog, Mr. Knight was telling us about his past adventures just now. In fact, he was right in the middle of a very interesting story when you came in. Would you like to stay a while and listen with us?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I'll pass on the ghost stories; I am very busy. However, I feel I must caution you, ladies.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: There exist people in this world whose mouths are incapable of speaking the truth. Not only do they spin their yarns, boasting about what has never truly transpired, but they may even shirk their responsibilities and force minors to carry out their work for them.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone doesn't even have a mouth! Although someone has been wondering for some time now—how does someone even speak without anything with which to speak out of?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Through the magic of your arcane skill!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I knew this was going to happen.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper? You came to visit, too? Did something happen to Mr. Fog today? He appears to be in quite a foul mood.
I don't think he's very happy about having to work outside of his schedule.
items.edge_label: 残業に対する抗議ってところかな

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: I see...
TO BE CONTINUED ...
